key_insight: TRAMA transfers knowledge from a cheap linear property into a reusable learned design space for optimizing nonlinear mechanical metamaterial behavior.
engineering_relevance: The approach reduces costly simulation-driven searches for energy-absorbing architectures, saving approximately 100 hours per finite-element optimization campaign.
method: Learn an architectural representation using a variational autoencoder with a pre-trained vision transformer.
Use physics-informed augmentations to support representation learning.
Transfer the learned search space to nonlinear, potentially non-differentiable design objectives.
evidence_signal: For energy-absorption efficiency, TRAMA required 95–98% fewer evaluations than state-of-the-art gradient-free optimization, while fabricated designs matched simulated stress–strain curves within 5.3%.
watch_item: Transferability is property-dependent; the learned representation may not benefit every new objective.
paper_title: Efficient Optimization of Mechanical Metamaterials via Transferable Representation Learning
